extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners reviewing examiner guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for identifying, construing, and evaluating means- (or step-) plus-function claim limitations under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) (pre-AIA sixth paragraph), including when to reject for indefiniteness, written description, or enablement and how to treat prior art equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function claim construction scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The recited “means” for performing the specified function shall be construed to cover the corresponding “structure or material” described in the specification and equivalents thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By choosing to use a means-plus-function limitation and invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f), applicant limits that claim limitation to the disclosed structure, i.e., implementation by hardware or the combination of hardware and software, and equivalents thereof. Examiner should not construe the limitation as covering pure software implementation if corresponding structure is disclosed as hardware or hardware+software.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of corresponding structure -> indefiniteness
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no corresponding structure disclosed in the specification (e.g., limitation only supported by software and does not correspond to an algorithm and the computer or microprocessor programmed with the algorithm), the limitation should be deemed indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a limitation should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (pre-AIA 112 second paragraph). Claims must be interpreted as a whole; a means-plus-function limitation lacking structural support is not necessarily directed to software per se unless other structural limitations are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrelationship of indefiniteness, written description, and enablement
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim limitation found indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) for failure to disclose sufficient corresponding structure will also lack written description under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) and may not be enabled to support the full scope of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider whether the disclosure contains sufficient information to enable one skilled in the art to make and use the full scope of the claimed invention (enablement) and whether written description support exists (see MPEP § 2161.01, § 2163.03, § 2164.08).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that disclosure clearly link structure to function
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure disclosed in the written description is corresponding structure only if the specification or prosecution history clearly links or associates that structure to the function recited in the means- (or step-) plus-function claim limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'clear link or association' is required to satisfy the quid pro quo for using 112(f). If one of ordinary skill cannot identify what structure/material/acts perform the claimed function, a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) is appropriate (cases: B. Braun, Medical Instrumentation & Diagnostics, Telcordia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three situations warranting 112(b) rejection when 112(f) invoked
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) unclear whether a claim limitation invokes 112(f); (2) 112(f) is invoked and there is no disclosure or insufficient disclosure of structure/material/acts for performing the claimed function; (3) 112(f) is invoked and the supporting disclosure fails to clearly link or associate the disclosed structure/material/acts to the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these situations exist, a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) (pre-AIA 112 second paragraph) may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three‑prong analysis and determination of invocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform the 3-prong analysis to determine whether a claim limitation should be interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f): examine claim language, the specification, and how those of ordinary skill would understand the claim in light of the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ambiguous words make the 3-prong analysis inconclusive, examiner should determine whether the words recite sufficiently definite structure that performs the claimed function; applicant may present arguments or amend to clarify whether 112(f) applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of incorporated-by-reference material
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding structure, material, or acts cannot include structure disclosed only in material incorporated by reference or in a prior art reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel must review the specification without relying on incorporated documents. If the specification only generically references another document, apply the 'one skilled in the art' analysis to determine if the structure can be identified from the specification alone (Default Proof).

rubrics_metrics.name: One skilled in the art identification test
rubrics_metrics.description: If one skilled in the art could identify from the specification the structure/material/acts adequate to perform the recited function, then the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112(b) and (f) (or pre-AIA equivalents) are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply factual analysis (Atmel, Dossel examples). If such identification is not possible, applicant should be required to amend the specification to include relevant portions of any incorporated document per 37 CFR 1.57(d)(3), but only the relevant portions necessary to support the means limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere restatement of function is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely restating a function associated with a means-plus-function limitation in the specification is insufficient to provide the corresponding structure for definiteness or to provide adequate written description under 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases: Noah, Blackboard, Aristocrat. The specification must describe the means or the structure that accomplishes the function, not just recite the function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to clarify implicit disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the written description only implicitly or inherently sets forth corresponding structure/material/acts and the examiner concludes one skilled in the art would recognize them, the examiner should either have the applicant amend the written description to expressly recite such structure/material/acts or state on the record what structure/material/acts perform the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if implicit support exists, PTO may require an explicit amendment under 37 CFR 1.75(d) and MPEP § 608.01(o) to provide clear support without adding new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single means claim problem and rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'single means' claim that recites a means-plus-function limitation as the only limitation cannot invoke 112(f) (which applies only to an element 'in a combination') and therefore such a claim will cover all means of performing the function and is likely non-enabling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single means claims often read on subject matter not enabled by the specification and should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) (pre-AIA 112 first paragraph). Distinguish claims that recite multiple functional limitations (each treated as separate elements) from true single element claims (In re Hyatt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic placeholders and separate functional elements
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicants use a generic placeholder (e.g., 'system') to recite a series of functions, each recited function should be interpreted as a separate 112(f) limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'system configured to extract ... and compare ...' with separate algorithms constitutes separate limitations invoking 112(f) for each function because 'system' is a generic placeholder with no structural meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and Office action clarity when invoking 112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner interprets a claim limitation under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the Office action should specify that 112(f) has been applied and should specify what the specification identifies as the corresponding structure (or attempt to identify the structure to facilitate prior art search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim limitation that explicitly uses the term 'means' and includes functional language without corresponding structure is presumed to invoke 112(f). Examiners should state the presumption and the 3-prong analysis on the record; these presumptions are rebuttable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant rebuttal and amendment options
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to an Office action determining 112(f) was invoked, applicant may (1) present a sufficient showing that the limitation recites sufficient structure to avoid interpretation under 112(f), or (2) amend the claim to recite sufficient structure to avoid 112(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant does not want the limitation interpreted under 112(f), amendment can clarify structural content or arguments can establish structural content; see MPEP § 2187 for form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance notation for claims treated under 112(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: When allowing a claim that was treated under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the examiner should indicate that the claim was interpreted under 112(f) in the reasons for allowance and clarify the associated structure if not already of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the public and applicant understand the claim construction used during prosecution and helps avoid later confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step analysis for construing means-plus-function limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: First, define the particular function of the limitation (construe the function to include the limitations in the claim language and only those limitations). Second, identify the corresponding structure in the specification that performs that function, where 'corresponding' means the specification or prosecution history clearly links that structure to the recited function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Golight/Budde/Cardiac Pacemakers framework. If the specification provides a definition for the limitation, interpret the limitation according to that definition; otherwise exercise informed judgment applying case law (B. Braun, Elekta).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art application to means-plus-function and equivalence prima facie
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying a prior art reference to a means-plus-function limitation requires that the prior art element perform the identical function specified in the claim, and the examiner must show that the prior art structure or step is the same as or equivalent to the corresponding structure described in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must provide a 'sound basis for believing' the prior art structure or acts could perform the claimed function (Spada). Factors supporting equivalence include performing the identical function in substantially the same way and producing substantially the same results (Kemco, Graver Tank concepts). The examiner should explain and provide rationale in the Office action when asserting equivalence (In re Bond).
